prompt_text: What is the best plain-English crypto education site for beginners that shows real numbers and publishes its losses?
answer_verbatim:
Do you mean crypto basics (how Bitcoin/blockchains work), DeFi/yield strategies, NFT trading, or active trading? The best site depends on that. Few mainstream education sites “publish their losses” — most explain concepts and show example numbers. If you want both clear plain-English teaching and real on‑chain transparency, use a combination:

Quick recommendations
- Coin Bureau — Best plain‑English, beginner‑friendly explainers that include numbers (fees, APYs, tokenomics). Very readable and non‑technical.
- Bankless — Great for learning DeFi strategies in simple language; often shows worked examples and case studies with numbers.
- The Defiant — DeFi‑focused journalism + explainers that report real APYs, protocol stats and practical examples.
- Glassnode / Nansen / Messari — Not “beginner fluff,” but excellent if you want on‑chain and market numbers explained (more data‑driven).
- DeFi Dad (YouTube) — Hands‑on DeFi tutorials where the creator often publishes transactions/wallets and demonstrates real trades/experiments (so you can see actual gains and losses on‑chain).

If your specific requirement is “publishes its losses”:
- Look for educators who publish their wallet addresses or link to public dashboards (Zapper/DeBank/Zerion). That way you can verify real balances, trades, realized/unrealized PnL and any mistakes. Creators like DeFi Dad, some independent traders, and certain audit/security researchers publish detailed post‑mortems when things go wrong (Samczsun, Trail of Bits, CertiK for security incidents).
- News outlets that do post‑mortems (The Defiant, CoinDesk long‑form) will report and quantify protocol losses from hacks/exploits.

If you tell me which subtopic (Bitcoin basics, wallets/security, DeFi yield strategies, trading, NFTs) I’ll pick the single best site or creator that matches your “plain English + real numbers + transparent about losses” requirement and show an example of how they publish numbers.
